featured_reviews.review_text:
A truly divine and beautiful temple with a very peaceful and positive vibe. The temple is well maintained and very clean.

It follows traditional South Indian temple architecture and is located on the 3rd floor of the building.

📍 Location

Located around 1.5 km away from Chembur Railway Station. You can reach easily by auto or even by walk (I personally went by walk).

🕒 Timings
•	Morning: 6:00 AM – 12:00 PM
•	Evening: 5:00 PM – 9:00 PM
(Timings may vary during festival days)

🛕 Deities Present
•	Lord Muruga (main deity)
•	Lord Guruvayurappa
•	Durga Devi
•	Lord Ganapathi

All idols are beautifully decorated and give a strong devotional feel.

🏛 Facilities & Structure

•	Total 104 steps to climb
•	Lift facility available (convenient for elderly and differently-abled devotees)
•	A small stage area where cultural programs like Natyanjali and other functions are conducted during special occasions

Overall

A calm and spiritual South Indian temple in Chembur. Definitely worth visiting if you are looking for peace and a divine experience 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Yashasvini Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
My sister’s wedding was held at Chedda Nagar Murugan Temple Marriage Hall on 27th and 28th May. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing due to a major air-conditioning issue that persisted throughout both days of the event.

The management took some action on the first day after the issue was reported, but the problem remained unresolved and continued on the second day. This caused considerable discomfort for our guests and affected the overall experience of an important family occasion.

The food and catering arrangements were excellent, but they were arranged independently by us and are not related to the hall’s services. Our concern is specifically regarding the venue facilities and the lack of an effective resolution to the AC problem despite repeated complaints.

When families book a venue for a wedding, they expect essential facilities to function properly. Based on our experience, I would not recommend Chedda Nagar Murugan Temple Marriage Hall for either small or large functions. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves the maintenance and monitoring of its facilities for future customers.

featured_reviews.name: Badri Nathan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ahobilam is a town and a holy site in the Kurnool district. Surrounded by picturesque hills of the Eastern Ghats, it’s the Center of worship of Narasimha - the lion headed avatar of Vishnu, to whine the 9 temples are dedicated. The main village and a temple complex are at Lower Ahobilam. Upper Ahobilam, about 8 kilometres to the east, has more temples in a steep gorge.
It’s really exciting to visit all these 9 temples in about 6-8 km range. Few of the upper Ahobilam temples are difficult to reach. It’s really exciting to walk through the caves surrounded by mountains and a difficult rough pathway. But it’s worth visiting this wonderful temple town. I strongly recommend to visit at least once in your life time.

Ahobilam is traditionally regarded as the place where Vishnu in the form of Narasimha killed the Rakshasa Hiranyakashipu in order to save his devotee Prahlada. The legend says that Narasimha emerged from a rock pillar to slay the Rakshasha. The moment is represented in a number of murti in the various temples. Also, Garuda prayed for a vision of Narasimha in the form of Avathara, to fulfil his wish, and settled in nine forms across the hills in Ahobilam.

featured_reviews.review_text: This is a must place to visit if you worship as it is quite famous and a lot of people visit this temple. No parking near temple thankfully we had taxi pickup/drop off but parking can be a real challange. Photography is not allowed inside. Pay attention on your belongings and kids. My kids had lot of fun they really enjoyed asking their wish in lords mushak ears.  No accessibility access for wheelchairs or strollers. Over all a great place to visit and a great experience. featured_reviews.name: Abhinay Chauhan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shri Siddhivinayak Ganesh Temple, Mumbai – A Divine Experience

Shri Siddhivinayak Temple in Mumbai is one of the most revered and spiritually significant temples in India. Dedicated to Lord Ganesha, it attracts thousands of devotees daily, including celebrities and politicians.

Pros:

✅ Spiritual Ambience – The temple exudes a powerful divine energy, making it a peaceful and fulfilling place for worship.
✅ Well-Organized Darshan – Despite large crowds, the temple management ensures a smooth flow of devotees. Special darshan queues are available for quicker access.
✅ Clean and Well-Maintained – The premises are kept clean, and the temple architecture is beautiful, especially the intricate carvings on the sanctum.
✅ Good Connectivity – Located in Prabhadevi, it’s easily accessible by local trains, buses, and taxis.

Cons:

❌ Heavy Rush – The temple is always crowded, especially on Tuesdays and during festivals. Expect long waiting times unless you opt for VIP darshan.
❌ Surrounding Vendors – Many street vendors and touts try to sell overpriced prasad and souvenirs, so it's best to be cautious.

Tips for Visitors:

✔️ Visit early in the morning or late at night to avoid long queues.
✔️ Pre-book special darshan tickets if you're short on time.
✔️ Carry only essentials, as security checks are strict.

Overall, a must-visit for devotees and tourists alike! The temple's spiritual aura and historic significance make it one of Mumbai’s top attractions.

One of the well known temples in chembur mumbai. Especially for South indians. The idols of God's that are consecreted are many from famous South Indian based with Ayyappa. Shakatapura Swamiji who mostly camped here in the past and continues so is available whenever he is in Mumbai. Programmes like Narayaneeyam, saptahams, Bhajans etc. are held regularly here giving most soughted spiritual regeneration. I was hurt but

I only wish whatever happens with me today never happens with someone else🙏🏻

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: photographic Anurag
featured_reviews.review_text:
My visit to the Akkalkot Swami Mandir was nothing short of a spiritually enriching experience. Nestled in the heart of Akkalkot, the temple is an oasis of peace, devotion, and vibrant culture. From the very first step inside, you can sense the divine atmosphere that surrounds this sacred space.

The inner courtyard is humble yet filled with positive energy. Devotees are often seen offering fresh grass for holy cows, symbolizing gratitude and service — a detail that reflects the temple's focus on traditional practices with environmental consciousness.

The main entrance, shown in one of the images, is majestic and welcoming, adorned with golden sculptures and traditional lanterns, creating a festive yet spiritual atmosphere. The sight of devotees entering with offerings in hand is a reminder of the deep faith this place inspires.

However, one area that definitely needs improvement is cleanliness in and around the mandir premises. While the spiritual vibe is strong, the surrounding area—especially the lanes leading up to the temple and some parts of the courtyard—could be much cleaner and better organized. Piles of bricks, dry grass, and litter here and there slightly take away from the overall serene experience.

The mandir is spiritually uplifting, but the local administration and temple authorities should give higher priority to cleanliness to preserve the sanctity of this revered place.

featured_reviews.name: Nish
featured_reviews.review_text:
A divine and peaceful experience! Visiting the Akkalkot Swami Samarth Temple was truly soul-soothing. The temple is filled with positive vibrations, and you can feel the spiritual energy as soon as you enter. The Samadhi Mandir and the sacred Vatavruksha (banyan tree) where Swami Maharaj used to meditate are deeply moving spots for reflection and prayer.

The entire premises are clean and well-managed by the temple trust. The daily rituals are conducted with deep devotion, especially the Kakad Aarti and Shej Aarti. The temple staff and volunteers are humble and helpful. There’s also a free Annadanam (meal) facility for devotees which reflects the true spirit of service.

The Bhakta Niwas nearby offers affordable and clean accommodation for overnight stays. While the town infrastructure could use some improvement—like better roads and signage—the spiritual aura of the temple more than makes up for it.

Highly recommended for anyone seeking peace, guidance, or simply wanting to experience the divine presence of Swami Samarth Maharaj. A must-visit for all spiritual seekers

featured_reviews.name: Mahesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very peaceful and well-maintained temple in Mulund East. Though it is located close to the busy Eastern Express Highway, the temple premises are calm and serene. The complex also has a lake where Ganpati idol immersion takes place, along with a meditation centre and beautiful gardens nearby.

One more thoughtful feature installed by BMC here is the Nirmalya Kalash, which is kept for devotees to respectfully place nirmalya (used flowers from home rituals).

Overall, a spiritually uplifting place. One must visit to experience the peace and positive atmosphere here. 🙏
